definition: the highest point; ideal or culminating example
memoryTip: Apo-theos: raised to godlike status—the peak or ideal.
correctPassage: Critics hailed the final movement as the apotheosis of the composer's lifelong work with form.
wrongPassages: The committee treated the unfinished draft as the apotheosis of a project still lacking direction.
After years of decline, the firm reached its apotheosis when sales hit their lowest recorded level.
Historians dated the apotheosis of the movement to the decade before it had any public influence.

definition: describing a work of visual art in literary form
memoryTip: Ekphrasis = words that re-paint art—a poem about a painting.
correctPassage: Her ekphrastic sequence answers the museum triptych stanza by stanza in carefully paced prose.
wrongPassages: The biologist's ekphrastic chart tracked enzyme rates without describing any painting or sculpture.
Reviewers called the purely fiscal brief ekphrastic even though it never engaged a work of visual art.
He delivered an ekphrastic inventory of warehouse stock, item by item, with no artistic subject.

definition: relating to an agent or the capacity to act
memoryTip: Agent-ial: about who can act—having agency.
correctPassage: The study emphasizes the agential role of local organizers in shaping the reform.
wrongPassages: Observers called the policy agential precisely because citizens had no room to choose or resist.
Critics found the protagonist agential only in the chapters where outside forces decided every outcome.
The dormant machinery was labeled agential while it remained powered down and untouched for months.

definition: the state of being annoyed or worried
correctPassage: Repeated schedule changes became a steady source of vexation for the research team.
wrongPassages: The quiet afternoon brought a rare vexation of ease that settled over the entire household.
She recalled the promotion with pure vexation, smiling at how perfectly everything had aligned.
The reunion filled him with vexation so complete he could not stop laughing in relief.

definition: words that imitate the sound they name
memoryTip: Buzz, hiss, boom—words that sound like what they mean.
correctPassage: In the graphic novel, each collision panel is edged with bold onomatopoeia that echoes the impact.
wrongPassages: The silent geometry treatise was praised for its onomatopoeia, though no word mimicked a sound.
She classified abstract ledger terms such as equity and liability as onomatopoeia.
His onomatopoeia chapter surveyed only color gradients and never a sound-imitating word.
